svg.title: Fig. 203(a) — The sine curve as the projection of a helix on a cylinder
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 203(a), page 229. Section: trigonometric.

g.data-text: The cylinder (its axis dash-dot) with the circumscribed box: the floor of the box is the plane onto which the helix will be projected, parallel to the axis.

The helix x = p·t, y = r cos t, z = r sin t on the cylinder: it cuts every element of the cylinder at the same angle. The half of each turn nearest the viewer is drawn solid, the half behind the cylinder dashed.
Drop perpendiculars from the helix to the floor (parallel to the axis): the feet make the thick curve y = r cos(x/p), a sine curve in the plane of the floor. One perpendicular is drawn dashed.
